segments.tr: Brand equity ≈ what people will pay for the branded version

segments.src: − what they'd pay for an identical unbranded version
segments.tr: − what they'd pay for an identical unbranded version

segments.src: That's a simplification (equity also shows up as loyalty, bargaining power with retailers, and cheaper customer acquisition), but it makes the idea concrete: equity is measurable, and it lives in the customer's mind, not on the factory floor.
segments.tr: Isso é uma simplificação (equity também aparece como lealdade, poder de negociação com varejistas e aquisição de clientes mais barata), mas torna a ideia concreta: equity é mensurável e vive na mente do cliente, não no chão de fábrica.

segments.src: Marketing academics usually break brand equity into four building blocks, following David Aaker's well-known model:
segments.tr: Os acadêmicos de marketing geralmente dividem brand equity em quatro blocos de construção, seguindo o modelo bem conhecido de David Aaker:

segments.src: - **Awareness** — do people know you exist, and do you come to mind first?
segments.tr: - **Awareness (Consciência)** — as pessoas sabem que você existe e você vem à mente primeiro?

segments.src: - **Perceived quality** — do they believe you're good, whether or not lab tests agree?
segments.tr: - **Perceived quality (Qualidade Percebida)** — eles acreditam que você é bom, quer os testes de laboratório concordem ou não?

segments.src: - **Associations** — what images, feelings, and situations attach to the name?
segments.tr: - **Associations (Associações)** — que imagens, sentimentos e situações se ligam ao nome?

segments.src: - **Loyalty** — will they buy you again when a cheaper option is right there?
segments.tr: - **Loyalty (Lealdade)** — eles comprarão você novamente quando uma opção mais barata estiver ali?

segments.src: Now, the second concept.
segments.tr: Agora, o segundo conceito.

segments.src: **Brand identity** is what the company *intends* the brand to stand for — the positioning, the personality, the visual system, the tone.
segments.tr: **Brand identity (Identidade de Marca)** é o que a empresa *pretende* que a marca represente — o posicionamento, a personalidade, o sistema visual, o tom.

segments.src: **Brand image** is what customers *actually* believe.
segments.tr: **Brand image (Imagem de Marca)** é o que os clientes *realmente* acreditam.

segments.src: Those two are rarely the same thing, and closing the gap is most of a brand manager's job.
segments.tr: Esses dois raramente são a mesma coisa, e fechar a lacuna é a maior parte do trabalho de um gerente de marca.

segments.src: You control the identity.
segments.tr: Você controla a identidade.

segments.src: You only influence the image.
segments.tr: Você apenas influencia a imagem.

segments.src: Third: **brand extension**.
segments.tr: Terceiro: **brand extension (extensão de marca)**.

segments.src: Once a brand has equity, it's tempting to spend it — to launch a product in a new category under the same name and borrow the trust you've already earned.
segments.tr: Uma vez que uma marca tem equity, é tentador gastá-la — lançar um produto em uma nova categoria sob o mesmo nome e pegar emprestado a confiança que você já conquistou.

segments.src: Extensions are cheap compared to building a brand from zero, and that's exactly why they're overused.
segments.tr: As extensões são baratas comparadas a construir uma marca do zero, e é exatamente por isso que são usadas em excesso.

segments.src: The variable that predicts success is **perceived fit**: does the new product feel like something this brand would plausibly make?
segments.tr: A variável que prediz sucesso é **perceived fit (encaixe percebido)**: o novo produto parece algo que essa marca faria plausivamente?

segments.src: Nike moving from shoes into athletic apparel fits.
segments.tr: Nike passando de sapatos para roupas esportivas encaixa.

segments.src: Apple moving from computers into phones fits.
segments.tr: Apple passando de computadores para telefones encaixa.

segments.src: Harley-Davidson launching a perfume in the 1990s did not fit, and it's still cited in textbooks as the cautionary tale.
segments.tr: Harley-Davidson lançando um perfume nos anos 1990 não encaixava, e ainda é citado em livros didáticos como a história de cautela.

segments.src: When fit is weak, the extension usually fails — and worse, it can cause **brand dilution**, muddying the associations that made the parent brand valuable in the first place.
segments.tr: Quando o encaixe é fraco, a extensão geralmente falha — e pior, pode causar **brand dilution (diluição de marca)**, confundindo as associações que tornaram a marca-mãe valiosa em primeiro lugar.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## Na Vida do Dia a Dia

segments.src: Stand in the pain-relief aisle at a CVS or a Walgreens.
segments.tr: Fique em pé na seção de alívio da dor em uma CVS ou uma Walgreens.

segments.src: On the shelf: Tylenol Extra Strength, 500 mg acetaminophen.
segments.tr: Na prateleira: Tylenol Extra Strength, 500 mg de acetaminofeno.

segments.src: Next to it: the store's own brand — CVS Health or Walgreens — also 500 mg acetaminophen.
segments.tr: Ao lado: a marca própria da loja — CVS Health ou Walgreens — também 500 mg de acetaminofeno.

segments.src: Same active ingredient, same dose, both regulated by the FDA to the same standard.
segments.tr: Mesmo ingrediente ativo, mesma dose, ambos regulados pela FDA para o mesmo padrão.

segments.src: The store brand often costs noticeably less per caplet; the exact spread moves with sales and store, but a several-dollar gap on a 100-count bottle is typical.
segments.tr: A marca da loja muitas vezes custa notavelmente menos por comprimido; o spread exato se move com vendas e loja, mas uma diferença de alguns dólares em um frasco de 100 comprimidos é típico.

segments.src: Millions of Americans reach for the more expensive one anyway.
segments.tr: Milhões de americanos pegam a mais cara mesmo assim.

segments.src: That decision, repeated at scale, *is* brand equity.
segments.tr: Essa decisão, repetida em escala, *é* brand equity.

segments.src: People aren't buying better chemistry.
segments.tr: As pessoas não estão comprando química melhor.

segments.src: They're buying a reduction in doubt — at 2 a.m., with a sick kid, when you don't want to be the person who experimented.
segments.tr: Eles estão comprando uma redução na dúvida — às 2 da manhã, com uma criança doente, quando você não quer ser a pessoa que experimentou.

segments.src: Some of that trust was earned in a specific moment.
segments.tr: Parte dessa confiança foi ganha em um momento específico.

segments.src: In 1982, seven people in the Chicago area died after someone laced Tylenol capsules with cyanide.
segments.tr: Em 1982, sete pessoas na área de Chicago morreram depois que alguém adulterou cápsulas de Tylenol com cianeto.

segments.src: Johnson & Johnson pulled roughly 31 million bottles nationwide, went public fast, and came back with tamper-evident packaging that became the industry norm.
segments.tr: Johnson & Johnson retirou aproximadamente 31 milhões de garrafas em todo o país, saiu à público rapidamente e voltou com embalagem à prova de violação que se tornou a norma da indústria.

segments.src: The brand lost most of its share and rebuilt it within about a year.
segments.tr: A marca perdeu a maior parte de sua participação e a reconstruiu em cerca de um ano.

segments.src: That's the double lesson: equity is fragile enough to nearly vanish in a week, and durable enough to be worth defending at enormous cost.
segments.tr: Essa é a lição dupla: equity é frágil o suficiente para desaparecer quase completamente em uma semana e durável o suficiente para valer a pena defender a um custo enorme.

segments.src: Now look one shelf over at the extensions: Tylenol PM.
segments.tr: Agora olhe uma prateleira acima as extensões: Tylenol PM.

segments.src: Tylenol Cold + Flu.
segments.tr: Tylenol Cold + Flu.

segments.src: Children's Tylenol.
segments.tr: Children's Tylenol.

segments.src: Every one of them is the same bet — *you already trust us with your headache, so trust us with your cold.* High perceived fit, so the borrowing works.
segments.tr: Cada um deles é a mesma aposta — *você já confia em nós com sua dor de cabeça, então confie em nós com seu resfriado.* Alto encaixe percebido, então o empréstimo funciona.

segments.src: Then ask yourself the honest question: would you buy Tylenol-brand energy drinks?
segments.tr: Então faça a si mesmo a pergunta honesta: você compraria bebidas energéticas com marca Tylenol?

segments.src: Same company, same trust, same shelf.
segments.tr: Mesma empresa, mesma confiança, mesma prateleira.

segments.src: But the fit collapses, and so would the extension.
segments.tr: Mas o encaixe desaba, e a extensão também.

segments.src: Tylenol means "makes discomfort go away safely."
segments.tr: Tylenol significa "faz o desconforto desaparecer com segurança."

segments.src: An energy drink means the opposite of sedation.
segments.tr: Uma bebida energética significa o oposto de sedação.

segments.src: The name would fight the product.
segments.tr: O nome lutaria contra o produto.

segments.src: ## Three-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## Recapitulação de Três Linhas

segments.src: 1. Brand equity is the value the name adds on top of the product — built from awareness, perceived quality, associations, and loyalty.
segments.tr: 1. Brand equity é o valor que o nome adiciona além do produto — construído a partir de awareness, perceived quality, associations e loyalty.

segments.src: 2. Brand identity is what you intend to mean; brand image is what customers actually think you mean, and the gap between them is the job.
segments.tr: 2. Brand identity é o que você pretende significar; brand image é o que os clientes realmente pensam que você significa, e a lacuna entre eles é o trabalho.

segments.src: 3. Brand extensions let you spend accumulated equity in a new category — profitable when perceived fit is high, dilutive when it isn't.
segments.tr: 3. Brand extensions deixam você gastar equity acumulado em uma nova categoria — lucrativo quando perceived fit é alto, diluitivo quando não é.

segments.src: ## ✅ Self-Quiz
segments.tr: ## ✅ Auto-Questionário

segments.src: **1.** A store-brand acetaminophen has the identical active ingredient and dose as the national brand, yet many shoppers pay more for the national brand.
segments.tr: **1.** Um acetaminofeno de marca de loja tem o ingrediente ativo idêntico e dose que a marca nacional, mas muitos compradores pagam mais pela marca nacional.

segments.src: This price premium is the clearest everyday evidence of:
segments.tr: Esse prêmio de preço é a evidência mais clara do dia a dia de:

segments.src: - A) Product differentiation through formulation
segments.tr: - A) Diferenciação de produto através de formulação

segments.src: - B) Brand equity
segments.tr: - B) Brand equity

segments.src: - C) A distribution advantage
segments.tr: - C) Uma vantagem de distribuição

segments.src: - D) Regulatory protection
segments.tr: - D) Proteção regulatória

segments.src: **2.** True or False: Brand identity and brand image mean the same thing.
segments.tr: **2.** Verdadeiro ou Falso: Brand identity e brand image significam a mesma coisa.

segments.src: **3.** A premium coffee brand launches branded ceramic mugs and travel tumblers.
segments.tr: **3.** Uma marca de café premium lança canecas de cerâmica com marca e copos de viagem.

segments.src: Compared with that same brand launching motor oil, the mug launch is more likely to succeed mainly because of:
segments.tr: Comparado com essa mesma marca lançando óleo de motor, o lançamento de caneca é mais provável de ter sucesso principalmente porque:

segments.src: - A) Lower manufacturing cost
segments.tr: - A) Menor custo de fabricação

segments.src: - B) Higher perceived fit with existing brand associations
segments.tr: - B) Maior encaixe percebido com associações de marca existentes

segments.src: - C) Stronger patent position
segments.tr: - C) Posição de patente mais forte

segments.src: - D) A larger addressable market
segments.tr: - D) Um mercado endereçável maior

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 Termos de Hoje

segments.src: - **Brand equity** — the added value a brand name gives a product beyond its functional attributes, visible as price premium, loyalty, and market power.
segments.tr: - **Brand equity** — o valor agregado que um nome de marca dá a um produto além de seus atributos funcionais, visível como prêmio de preço, lealdade e poder de mercado.

segments.src: - **Brand identity** — the meaning and personality the company deliberately builds and wants the brand to stand for.
segments.tr: - **Brand identity** — o significado e a personalidade que a empresa deliberadamente constrói e quer que a marca represente.

segments.src: - **Brand image** — the meaning customers actually hold in their heads, which may differ from the intended identity.
segments.tr: - **Brand image** — o significado que os clientes realmente têm em suas cabeças, que pode diferir da identidade pretendida.

segments.src: - **Brand extension** — launching a product in a *new* category under an existing brand name (versus a **line extension**, a new variant inside the same category).
segments.tr: - **Brand extension** — lançar um produto em uma *nova* categoria sob um nome de marca existente (versus uma **line extension**, uma nova variante dentro da mesma categoria).

segments.src: - **Brand dilution** — the weakening of a brand's core associations, typically caused by extensions that don't fit or by inconsistent quality.
segments.tr: - **Brand dilution** — o enfraquecimento das associações principais de uma marca, tipicamente causado por extensões que não encaixam ou por qualidade inconsistente.

segments.src: *Answers: **1 — B.** With the active ingredient, dose, and regulatory standard held constant, the leftover willingness to pay is attributable to the name itself; that's the price-premium view of brand equity.
segments.tr: *Respostas: **1 — B.** Com o ingrediente ativo, dose e padrão regulatório mantidos constantes, a disposição restante de pagar é atribuível ao próprio nome; essa é a visão de prêmio de preço do brand equity.

segments.src: **2 — False.** Identity is sender-side (what the firm intends); image is receiver-side (what the customer perceives).
segments.tr: **2 — Falso.** Identidade é do lado do remetente (o que a empresa pretende); imagem é do lado do receptor (o que o cliente percebe).

segments.src: Managing a brand largely means shrinking the distance between the two.
segments.tr: Gerenciar uma marca significa em grande parte encolher a distância entre os dois.

segments.src: **3 — B.** Mugs and tumblers sit naturally inside a coffee brand's existing associations, so consumers transfer trust easily.
segments.tr: **3 — B.** Canecas e copos de viagem se encaixam naturalmente nas associações existentes de uma marca de café, então os consumidores transferem confiança facilmente.

segments.src: Motor oil shares no meaningful associations with coffee, so the transfer fails and risks diluting the parent brand.*
segments.tr: Óleo de motor não compartilha associações significativas com café, então a transferência falha e arrisca diluir a marca-mãe.*

in.title: [Marketing 101 #11] Mengapa Pil yang Sama Biayanya Dua Kali Lebih Mahal Ketika Ada Nama di Atasnya

segments.src: > A brand is a promise stored in someone's head — and brand management is the work of building that promise, keeping it consistent, and knowing how far you can stretch it before it snaps.
segments.tr: > Merek adalah janji yang tersimpan di benak seseorang — dan manajemen merek adalah pekerjaan membangun janji itu, menjaganya tetap konsisten, dan mengetahui seberapa jauh Anda dapat meregangkannya sebelum putus.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Konsep Hari Ini

segments.src: Walk into any store and you'll find two products that are physically close to identical, sitting side by side, with very different price tags.
segments.tr: Masuk ke toko mana pun dan Anda akan menemukan dua produk yang secara fisik hampir identik, berdampingan, dengan harga yang sangat berbeda.

segments.src: Nothing about the atoms explains the gap.
segments.tr: Tidak ada yang tentang atom yang menjelaskan perbedaannya.

segments.src: Something about the *name* does.
segments.tr: Sesuatu tentang *nama* yang menjelaskannya.

segments.src: That gap has a name in marketing: **brand equity** — the extra value a brand name adds beyond what the product itself delivers.
segments.tr: Perbedaan itu memiliki nama dalam pemasaran: **ekuitas merek** — nilai tambah yang ditambahkan nama merek di luar apa yang disampaikan produk itu sendiri.

segments.src: One rough way to picture it:
segments.tr: Satu cara kasar untuk membayangkannya:

segments.src: Brand equity ≈ what people will pay for the branded version
segments.tr: Brand equity ≈ what people will pay for the branded version

segments.src: − what they'd pay for an identical unbranded version
segments.tr: − what they'd pay for an identical unbranded version

segments.src: That's a simplification (equity also shows up as loyalty, bargaining power with retailers, and cheaper customer acquisition), but it makes the idea concrete: equity is measurable, and it lives in the customer's mind, not on the factory floor.
segments.tr: Itu adalah penyederhanaan (ekuitas juga muncul sebagai loyalitas, kekuatan tawar dengan pengecer, dan akuisisi pelanggan yang lebih murah), tetapi hal itu membuat idenya konkret: ekuitas dapat diukur, dan ia hidup di pikiran pelanggan, bukan di lantai pabrik.

segments.src: Marketing academics usually break brand equity into four building blocks, following David Aaker's well-known model:
segments.tr: Akademisi pemasaran biasanya membagi ekuitas merek menjadi empat blok bangunan, mengikuti model terkenal David Aaker:

segments.src: - **Awareness** — do people know you exist, and do you come to mind first?
segments.tr: - **Kesadaran** — apakah orang tahu Anda ada, dan apakah Anda muncul pertama kali di benak?

segments.src: - **Perceived quality** — do they believe you're good, whether or not lab tests agree?
segments.tr: - **Kualitas yang Dirasakan** — apakah mereka percaya Anda baik, terlepas dari apakah tes lab setuju atau tidak?

segments.src: - **Associations** — what images, feelings, and situations attach to the name?
segments.tr: - **Asosiasi** — gambar, perasaan, dan situasi apa yang melekat pada nama?

segments.src: - **Loyalty** — will they buy you again when a cheaper option is right there?
segments.tr: - **Loyalitas** — akankah mereka membeli Anda lagi ketika ada pilihan yang lebih murah di sana?

segments.src: Now, the second concept.
segments.tr: Sekarang, konsep kedua.

segments.src: **Brand identity** is what the company *intends* the brand to stand for — the positioning, the personality, the visual system, the tone.
segments.tr: **Identitas merek** adalah apa yang *dimaksudkan* perusahaan agar merek berdiri untuk — positioning, kepribadian, sistem visual, nada.

segments.src: **Brand image** is what customers *actually* believe.
segments.tr: **Citra merek** adalah apa yang *sebenarnya* diyakini pelanggan.

segments.src: Those two are rarely the same thing, and closing the gap is most of a brand manager's job.
segments.tr: Keduanya jarang hal yang sama, dan menutup kesenjangan adalah sebagian besar pekerjaan manajer merek.

segments.src: You control the identity.
segments.tr: Anda mengontrol identitasnya.

segments.src: You only influence the image.
segments.tr: Anda hanya mempengaruhi citra.

segments.src: Third: **brand extension**.
segments.tr: Ketiga: **perluasan merek**.

segments.src: Once a brand has equity, it's tempting to spend it — to launch a product in a new category under the same name and borrow the trust you've already earned.
segments.tr: Setelah merek memiliki ekuitas, sudah menggoda untuk menghabiskannya — meluncurkan produk di kategori baru dengan nama yang sama dan meminjam kepercayaan yang sudah Anda peroleh.

segments.src: Extensions are cheap compared to building a brand from zero, and that's exactly why they're overused.
segments.tr: Perluasan itu murah dibandingkan dengan membangun merek dari nol, dan itu persis mengapa mereka sering digunakan berlebihan.

segments.src: The variable that predicts success is **perceived fit**: does the new product feel like something this brand would plausibly make?
segments.tr: Variabel yang memprediksi keberhasilan adalah **kesesuaian yang dirasakan**: apakah produk baru terasa seperti sesuatu yang secara wajar akan dibuat merek ini?

segments.src: Nike moving from shoes into athletic apparel fits.
segments.tr: Nike bergerak dari sepatu ke pakaian atletik cocok.

segments.src: Apple moving from computers into phones fits.
segments.tr: Apple bergerak dari komputer ke ponsel cocok.

segments.src: Harley-Davidson launching a perfume in the 1990s did not fit, and it's still cited in textbooks as the cautionary tale.
segments.tr: Harley-Davidson meluncurkan parfum pada tahun 1990an tidak cocok, dan masih dikutip dalam buku pelajaran sebagai kisah peringatan.

segments.src: When fit is weak, the extension usually fails — and worse, it can cause **brand dilution**, muddying the associations that made the parent brand valuable in the first place.
segments.tr: Ketika kesesuaiannya lemah, perluasan biasanya gagal — dan lebih buruk lagi, hal itu dapat menyebabkan **dilusi merek**, mengaburkan asosiasi yang membuat merek induk berharga sejak awal.

segments.src: Now look one shelf over at the extensions: Tylenol PM.

segments.src: ## Three-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## Ringkasan Tiga Baris

segments.src: 1. Brand equity is the value the name adds on top of the product — built from awareness, perceived quality, associations, and loyalty.
segments.tr: 1. Ekuitas merek adalah nilai yang ditambahkan nama di atas produk — dibangun dari kesadaran, kualitas yang dirasakan, asosiasi, dan loyalitas.

segments.src: 2. Brand identity is what you intend to mean; brand image is what customers actually think you mean, and the gap between them is the job.
segments.tr: 2. Identitas merek adalah apa yang Anda maksudkan; citra merek adalah apa yang benar-benar dipikirkan pelanggan Anda, dan celah di antara keduanya adalah pekerjaannya.

segments.src: 3. Brand extensions let you spend accumulated equity in a new category — profitable when perceived fit is high, dilutive when it isn't.
segments.tr: 3. Perluasan merek memungkinkan Anda menghabiskan ekuitas yang terkumpul di kategori baru — menguntungkan ketika kesesuaian yang dirasakan tinggi, bersifat dilutif ketika tidak.

segments.tr: ## ✅ Kuis Mandiri

segments.src: **1.** A store-brand acetaminophen has the identical active ingredient and dose as the national brand, yet many shoppers pay more for the national brand.

segments.tr: - A) Diferensiasi produk melalui formulasi

segments.tr: - B) Ekuitas merek

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 Istilah Hari Ini

segments.src: - **Brand equity** — the added value a brand name gives a product beyond its functional attributes, visible as price premium, loyalty, and market power.
segments.tr: - **Ekuitas merek** — nilai tambah yang diberikan nama merek ke produk di luar atribut fungsionalnya, terlihat sebagai premi harga, loyalitas, dan kekuatan pasar.

segments.src: - **Brand identity** — the meaning and personality the company deliberately builds and wants the brand to stand for.
segments.tr: - **Identitas merek** — makna dan kepribadian yang secara sengaja dibangun oleh perusahaan dan ingin merek berdiri untuk.

segments.src: - **Brand image** — the meaning customers actually hold in their heads, which may differ from the intended identity.
segments.tr: - **Citra merek** — makna yang sebenarnya dimiliki pelanggan di kepala mereka, yang mungkin berbeda dari identitas yang dimaksudkan.

segments.src: - **Brand extension** — launching a product in a *new* category under an existing brand name (versus a **line extension**, a new variant inside the same category).
segments.tr: - **Perluasan merek** — meluncurkan produk di kategori *baru* di bawah nama merek yang ada (versus **perluasan lini**, varian baru di dalam kategori yang sama).

segments.src: - **Brand dilution** — the weakening of a brand's core associations, typically caused by extensions that don't fit or by inconsistent quality.
segments.tr: - **Dilusi merek** — melemahnya asosiasi inti merek, biasanya disebabkan oleh perluasan yang tidak cocok atau oleh kualitas yang tidak konsisten.

segments.src: *Answers: **1 — B.** With the active ingredient, dose, and regulatory standard held constant, the leftover willingness to pay is attributable to the name itself; that's the price-premium view of brand equity.
segments.tr: *Jawaban: **1 — B.** Dengan bahan aktif, dosis, dan standar regulasi dipegang konstan, kesediaan membayar sisa dapat dikaitkan dengan nama itu sendiri; itu adalah pandangan premi harga dari ekuitas merek.

segments.src: **2 — False.** Identity is sender-side (what the firm intends); image is receiver-side (what the customer perceives).
segments.tr: **2 — Salah.** Identitas adalah sisi pengirim (apa yang dimaksudkan perusahaan); citra adalah sisi penerima (apa yang dirasakan pelanggan).

segments.src: Managing a brand largely means shrinking the distance between the two.
segments.tr: Mengelola merek sebagian besar berarti memperkecil jarak di antara keduanya.

segments.src: **3 — B.** Mugs and tumblers sit naturally inside a coffee brand's existing associations, so consumers transfer trust easily.
segments.tr: **3 — B.** Cangkir dan gelas duduk secara alami di dalam asosiasi merek kopi yang ada, jadi konsumen dengan mudah mentransfer kepercayaan.

segments.src: Motor oil shares no meaningful associations with coffee, so the transfer fails and risks diluting the parent brand.*
segments.tr: Minyak motor tidak memiliki asosiasi yang berarti dengan kopi, jadi transfer gagal dan berisiko mengencerkan merek induk.*

ja.title: [マーケティング 101 #11] 同じ薬が名前がついているだけで2倍の値段になるのはなぜか

segments.src: > A brand is a promise stored in someone's head — and brand management is the work of building that promise, keeping it consistent, and knowing how far you can stretch it before it snaps.
segments.tr: > ブランドとは誰かの頭の中に保存された約束であり、ブランド管理とはその約束を築き、一貫性を保ち、どこまで伸ばせるかを知ることの仕事です。

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## 本日のコンセプト

segments.src: Walk into any store and you'll find two products that are physically close to identical, sitting side by side, with very different price tags.
segments.tr: どのお店に行っても、物理的にほぼ同じ2つの製品が並んでいるのに、まったく異なる値段がついているのを見つけることができます。

segments.src: Nothing about the atoms explains the gap.
segments.tr: 原子のレベルではその差を説明することはできません。

segments.src: Something about the *name* does.
segments.tr: *名前*が説明します。

segments.src: That gap has a name in marketing: **brand equity** — the extra value a brand name adds beyond what the product itself delivers.
segments.tr: その差にはマーケティング用語があります：**ブランド・エクイティ**—ブランド名が製品自体が提供するもの以上に追加する余分な価値。

segments.src: One rough way to picture it:
segments.tr: それを想像する1つの大まかな方法：

segments.src: Brand equity ≈ what people will pay for the branded version
segments.tr: Brand equity ≈ what people will pay for the branded version

segments.src: − what they'd pay for an identical unbranded version
segments.tr: − what they'd pay for an identical unbranded version

segments.src: That's a simplification (equity also shows up as loyalty, bargaining power with retailers, and cheaper customer acquisition), but it makes the idea concrete: equity is measurable, and it lives in the customer's mind, not on the factory floor.
segments.tr: これは簡略化です（エクイティはまた忠誠度、小売業者との交渉力、より安い顧客獲得としても現れます）が、それは考えを具体的にします：エクイティは測定可能であり、顧客の心の中に存在し、工場の床ではありません。

segments.src: Marketing academics usually break brand equity into four building blocks, following David Aaker's well-known model:
segments.tr: マーケティング学者は通常、David Aaker の有名なモデルに基づいて、ブランド・エクイティを4つの構成要素に分けます：

segments.src: - **Awareness** — do people know you exist, and do you come to mind first?
segments.tr: - **認識**—人々はあなたが存在することを知っていますか、そしてあなたは最初に思い出されますか？

segments.src: - **Perceived quality** — do they believe you're good, whether or not lab tests agree?
segments.tr: - **知覚品質**—ラボテストが同意しているかどうかに関わらず、彼らはあなたが良いと信じていますか？

segments.src: - **Associations** — what images, feelings, and situations attach to the name?
segments.tr: - **連想**—どのようなイメージ、感情、状況が名前に関連付けられていますか？

segments.src: - **Loyalty** — will they buy you again when a cheaper option is right there?
segments.tr: - **忠誠心**—より安いオプションがすぐそこにあるとき、彼らは再度あなたを買いますか？

segments.src: Now, the second concept.
segments.tr: さて、2番目のコンセプトです。

segments.src: **Brand identity** is what the company *intends* the brand to stand for — the positioning, the personality, the visual system, the tone.
segments.tr: **ブランド・アイデンティティ**は、企業がブランドに*意図する*意味—ポジショニング、パーソナリティ、ビジュアルシステム、トーン。

segments.src: **Brand image** is what customers *actually* believe.
segments.tr: **ブランド・イメージ**は、顧客が*実際に*信じていることです。

segments.src: Those two are rarely the same thing, and closing the gap is most of a brand manager's job.
segments.tr: この2つが同じものになることはめったにありませんし、その差を埋めることがブランドマネージャーの仕事のほとんどです。

segments.src: You control the identity.
segments.tr: あなたはアイデンティティを制御します。

segments.src: You only influence the image.
segments.tr: あなたはイメージにのみ影響を及ぼします。

segments.src: Third: **brand extension**.
segments.tr: 3番目：**ブランド・エクステンション**。

segments.src: Once a brand has equity, it's tempting to spend it — to launch a product in a new category under the same name and borrow the trust you've already earned.
segments.tr: ブランドがエクイティを持つようになると、それを使いたくなります—同じ名前で新しいカテゴリーの製品を発売し、すでに獲得した信頼を借ります。

segments.src: Extensions are cheap compared to building a brand from zero, and that's exactly why they're overused.
segments.tr: エクステンションはブランドをゼロから構築することと比較して安いですし、それはまさに過度に使用されている理由です。

segments.src: The variable that predicts success is **perceived fit**: does the new product feel like something this brand would plausibly make?
segments.tr: 成功を予測する変数は**知覚フィット**です：新しい製品はこのブランドがもっともらしく作るものに感じられますか？

segments.src: Nike moving from shoes into athletic apparel fits.
segments.tr: ナイキが靴からアスレティックアパレルに移行するのはフィットします。

segments.src: Apple moving from computers into phones fits.
segments.tr: アップルがコンピューターから携帯電話に移行するのはフィットします。

segments.src: Harley-Davidson launching a perfume in the 1990s did not fit, and it's still cited in textbooks as the cautionary tale.
segments.tr: ハーレー・ダビッドソンが1990年代に香水を発売したのはフィットしなかった、そしてそれはまだ教科書で注意物語として引用されています。

segments.src: When fit is weak, the extension usually fails — and worse, it can cause **brand dilution**, muddying the associations that made the parent brand valuable in the first place.
segments.tr: フィットが弱い場合、エクステンションは通常失敗します—さらに悪いことに、**ブランド希薄化**を引き起こす可能性があり、最初に親ブランドを価値あるものにした連想を曖昧にします。

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## 日常生活で

segments.src: Stand in the pain-relief aisle at a CVS or a Walgreens.
segments.tr: CVSまたはWalgreensの鎮痛薬の売り場に立ってみてください。

segments.src: On the shelf: Tylenol Extra Strength, 500 mg acetaminophen.
segments.tr: 棚の上：Tylenol Extra Strength、500 mgアセトアミノフェン。

segments.src: Next to it: the store's own brand — CVS Health or Walgreens — also 500 mg acetaminophen.
segments.tr: その隣：店独自のブランド—CVS HealthまたはWalgreens—も500 mgアセトアミノフェン。

segments.src: Same active ingredient, same dose, both regulated by the FDA to the same standard.
segments.tr: 同じ有効成分、同じ用量、両方ともFDAによって同じ基準に規制されています。

segments.src: The store brand often costs noticeably less per caplet; the exact spread moves with sales and store, but a several-dollar gap on a 100-count bottle is typical.
segments.tr: 店のブランドは通常1錠あたり著しく安い価格です；正確なスプレッドは販売と店によって変動しますが、100個入りボトルで数ドルのギャップは一般的です。

segments.src: Millions of Americans reach for the more expensive one anyway.
segments.tr: 何百万ものアメリカ人はとにかくより高価な方を買います。

segments.src: That decision, repeated at scale, *is* brand equity.
segments.tr: その決定が規模で繰り返されることは*ブランド・エクイティです。*

segments.src: People aren't buying better chemistry.
segments.tr: 人々はより良い化学物質を買っているのではありません。

segments.src: They're buying a reduction in doubt — at 2 a.m., with a sick kid, when you don't want to be the person who experimented.
segments.tr: 彼らは疑いの軽減を買っています—午前2時に、病気の子供と一緒に、あなたが実験した人になりたくないとき。

segments.src: Some of that trust was earned in a specific moment.
segments.tr: その信頼の一部は特定の瞬間に獲得されました。

segments.src: In 1982, seven people in the Chicago area died after someone laced Tylenol capsules with cyanide.
segments.tr: 1982年、シカゴ地域の7人が、誰かがタイレノール・カプセルにシアン化物を混ぜた後に亡くなりました。

segments.src: Johnson & Johnson pulled roughly 31 million bottles nationwide, went public fast, and came back with tamper-evident packaging that became the industry norm.
segments.tr: ジョンソン・エンド・ジョンソンは全国で約31百万本を引き出し、急速に公開し、業界基準となった改ざん防止パッケージで戻ってきました。

segments.src: The brand lost most of its share and rebuilt it within about a year.
segments.tr: ブランドはそのシェアのほとんどを失い、約1年以内にそれを再構築しました。

segments.src: That's the double lesson: equity is fragile enough to nearly vanish in a week, and durable enough to be worth defending at enormous cost.
segments.tr: それは二つの教訓です：エクイティは1週間でほぼ消えるほど脆弱であり、莫大なコストで防御する価値があるほど耐久性があります。

segments.src: Now look one shelf over at the extensions: Tylenol PM.
segments.tr: さて、エクステンションをもう1つの棚越しに見てください：Tylenol PM。

segments.src: Tylenol Cold + Flu.
segments.tr: Tylenol Cold + Flu。

segments.src: Children's Tylenol.
segments.tr: 子供用Tylenol。

segments.src: Every one of them is the same bet — *you already trust us with your headache, so trust us with your cold.* High perceived fit, so the borrowing works.
segments.tr: それらのすべては同じ賭けです—*あなたはすでにあなたの頭痛で私たちを信頼しているので、あなたの風邪で私たちを信頼してください。*高い知覚フィット、だから借用が機能します。

segments.src: Then ask yourself the honest question: would you buy Tylenol-brand energy drinks?
segments.tr: 次に、正直な質問を自問してください：あなたはタイレノール・ブランドのエネルギードリンクを購入しますか？

segments.src: Same company, same trust, same shelf.
segments.tr: 同じ会社、同じ信頼、同じ棚。

segments.src: But the fit collapses, and so would the extension.
segments.tr: しかし、フィットは崩壊し、エクステンションも同様に崩壊します。

segments.src: Tylenol means "makes discomfort go away safely."
segments.tr: タイレノールは「不快感を安全に取り除く」という意味です。

segments.src: An energy drink means the opposite of sedation.
segments.tr: エネルギードリンクは鎮静の反対を意味します。

segments.src: The name would fight the product.
segments.tr: その名前は製品と矛盾するでしょう。

segments.src: ## Three-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## 3行の要約

segments.src: 1. Brand equity is the value the name adds on top of the product — built from awareness, perceived quality, associations, and loyalty.
segments.tr: 1. ブランド・エクイティは、名前が製品の上に追加する価値—認識、知覚品質、連想、忠誠度から構築されます。

segments.src: 2. Brand identity is what you intend to mean; brand image is what customers actually think you mean, and the gap between them is the job.
segments.tr: 2. ブランド・アイデンティティはあなたが意図する意味です；ブランド・イメージは顧客が実際にあなたが意図する意味です、そしてそれらの間のギャップは仕事です。

segments.src: 3. Brand extensions let you spend accumulated equity in a new category — profitable when perceived fit is high, dilutive when it isn't.
segments.tr: 3. ブランド・エクステンションは新しいカテゴリーで蓄積されたエクイティを使うことができます—知覚フィットが高い場合は利益が、そうでない場合は希薄化です。

segments.tr: **2.**真か偽：ブランド・アイデンティティとブランド・イメージは同じことを意味します。

segments.src: **3.** A premium coffee brand launches branded ceramic mugs and travel tumblers.

de.title: [Marketing 101 #11] Warum die gleiche Pille mit Markenname doppelt so viel kostet

segments.src: > A brand is a promise stored in someone's head — and brand management is the work of building that promise, keeping it consistent, and knowing how far you can stretch it before it snaps.
segments.tr: > Eine Marke ist ein Versprechen, das im Kopf eines Menschen gespeichert ist — und Markenmanagement ist die Arbeit, dieses Versprechen aufzubauen, es konsistent zu halten und zu wissen, wie weit man es dehnen kann, bevor es reißt.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Das Konzept von heute

segments.src: Walk into any store and you'll find two products that are physically close to identical, sitting side by side, with very different price tags.
segments.tr: Gehen Sie in ein beliebiges Geschäft und Sie werden zwei Produkte finden, die sich physisch kaum unterscheiden und nebeneinander mit völlig unterschiedlichen Preisschildern stehen.

segments.src: Nothing about the atoms explains the gap.
segments.tr: Nichts an den Atomen erklärt die Lücke.

segments.src: Something about the *name* does.
segments.tr: Etwas über den *Namen* tut es.

segments.src: That gap has a name in marketing: **brand equity** — the extra value a brand name adds beyond what the product itself delivers.
segments.tr: Diese Lücke hat einen Namen im Marketing: **Markenwert** — der zusätzliche Wert, den ein Markenname über das hinaus hinzufügt, was das Produkt selbst bietet.

segments.src: One rough way to picture it:
segments.tr: Eine grobe Methode, um es sich vorzustellen:

segments.src: Brand equity ≈ what people will pay for the branded version
segments.tr: Brand equity ≈ what people will pay for the branded version

segments.src: − what they'd pay for an identical unbranded version
segments.tr: − what they'd pay for an identical unbranded version

segments.src: That's a simplification (equity also shows up as loyalty, bargaining power with retailers, and cheaper customer acquisition), but it makes the idea concrete: equity is measurable, and it lives in the customer's mind, not on the factory floor.
segments.tr: Das ist eine Vereinfachung (Markenwert zeigt sich auch in Loyalität, Verhandlungsmacht bei Einzelhändlern und günstigerer Kundenakquisition), aber es macht die Idee konkret: Markenwert ist messbar und lebt im Kopf des Kunden, nicht auf dem Fabrikboden.

segments.src: Marketing academics usually break brand equity into four building blocks, following David Aaker's well-known model:
segments.tr: Marketingwissenschaftler teilen Markenwert normalerweise in vier Bausteine auf, nach dem bekannten Modell von David Aaker:

segments.src: - **Awareness** — do people know you exist, and do you come to mind first?
segments.tr: - **Bekanntheit** — kennen die Menschen Sie, und fallen Sie ihnen zuerst ein?

segments.src: - **Perceived quality** — do they believe you're good, whether or not lab tests agree?
segments.tr: - **Wahrgenommene Qualität** — glauben sie, dass Sie gut sind, unabhängig davon, ob Labortests zustimmen?

segments.src: - **Associations** — what images, feelings, and situations attach to the name?
segments.tr: - **Assoziationen** — welche Bilder, Gefühle und Situationen verbinden sich mit dem Namen?

segments.src: - **Loyalty** — will they buy you again when a cheaper option is right there?
segments.tr: - **Loyalität** — werden sie Sie wieder kaufen, wenn es eine günstigere Option gibt?

segments.src: Now, the second concept.
segments.tr: Jetzt das zweite Konzept.

segments.src: **Brand identity** is what the company *intends* the brand to stand for — the positioning, the personality, the visual system, the tone.
segments.tr: **Markenidentität** ist, wofür das Unternehmen *beabsichtigt*, dass die Marke steht — die Positionierung, die Persönlichkeit, das visuelle System, der Ton.

segments.src: **Brand image** is what customers *actually* believe.
segments.tr: **Markenimage** ist, was Kunden *tatsächlich* glauben.

segments.src: Those two are rarely the same thing, and closing the gap is most of a brand manager's job.
segments.tr: Diese beiden sind selten dasselbe, und die Lücke zu schließen ist der Großteil der Arbeit eines Markenmanagers.

segments.src: You control the identity.
segments.tr: Sie kontrollieren die Identität.

segments.src: You only influence the image.
segments.tr: Sie beeinflussen nur das Image.

segments.src: Third: **brand extension**.
segments.tr: Drittens: **Markenerweiterung**.

segments.src: Once a brand has equity, it's tempting to spend it — to launch a product in a new category under the same name and borrow the trust you've already earned.
segments.tr: Sobald eine Marke Markenwert hat, ist es verlockend, diesen auszugeben — ein Produkt in einer neuen Kategorie unter demselben Namen zu starten und das bereits verdiente Vertrauen zu nutzen.

segments.src: Extensions are cheap compared to building a brand from zero, and that's exactly why they're overused.
segments.tr: Erweiterungen sind billig im Vergleich zum Aufbau einer Marke von Grund auf, und genau deshalb werden sie zu viel genutzt.

segments.src: The variable that predicts success is **perceived fit**: does the new product feel like something this brand would plausibly make?
segments.tr: Die Variable, die den Erfolg vorhersagt, ist **wahrgenommene Passung**: fühlt sich das neue Produkt wie etwas an, das diese Marke plausiblerweise machen würde?

segments.src: Nike moving from shoes into athletic apparel fits.
segments.tr: Nike, das von Schuhen zu Sportkleidung übergeht, passt.

segments.src: Apple moving from computers into phones fits.
segments.tr: Apple, das von Computern zu Telefonen übergeht, passt.

segments.src: Harley-Davidson launching a perfume in the 1990s did not fit, and it's still cited in textbooks as the cautionary tale.
segments.tr: Harley-Davidson, das in den 1990er Jahren ein Parfüm startet, passte nicht, und es wird immer noch in Lehrbüchern als warnendes Beispiel angeführt.

segments.src: When fit is weak, the extension usually fails — and worse, it can cause **brand dilution**, muddying the associations that made the parent brand valuable in the first place.
segments.tr: Wenn die Passung schwach ist, schlägt die Erweiterung normalerweise fehl — und schlimmer noch, sie kann **Markenverwässerung** verursachen, die Assoziationen trüben, die die Muttermarke zunächst wertvoll machten.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## Im Alltag

segments.src: Stand in the pain-relief aisle at a CVS or a Walgreens.
segments.tr: Stehen Sie in der Schmerzmittelabteilung bei CVS oder Walgreens.

segments.src: On the shelf: Tylenol Extra Strength, 500 mg acetaminophen.
segments.tr: Im Regal: Tylenol Extra Strength, 500 mg Acetaminophen.

segments.src: Next to it: the store's own brand — CVS Health or Walgreens — also 500 mg acetaminophen.
segments.tr: Daneben: die Eigenmarke des Geschäfts — CVS Health oder Walgreens — ebenfalls 500 mg Acetaminophen.

segments.src: Same active ingredient, same dose, both regulated by the FDA to the same standard.
segments.tr: Gleicher Wirkstoff, gleiche Dosis, beide von der FDA zum gleichen Standard reguliert.

segments.src: The store brand often costs noticeably less per caplet; the exact spread moves with sales and store, but a several-dollar gap on a 100-count bottle is typical.
segments.tr: Die Eigenmarke kostet oft deutlich weniger pro Tablette; der genaue Unterschied variiert je nach Verkauf und Geschäft, aber ein Unterschied von mehreren Dollar bei einer Flasche mit 100 Stück ist typisch.

segments.src: Millions of Americans reach for the more expensive one anyway.
segments.tr: Millionen von Amerikanern greifen trotzdem zur teureren.

segments.src: That decision, repeated at scale, *is* brand equity.
segments.tr: Diese Entscheidung, im großen Maßstab wiederholt, *ist* Markenwert.

segments.src: People aren't buying better chemistry.
segments.tr: Menschen kaufen keine bessere Chemie.

segments.src: They're buying a reduction in doubt — at 2 a.m., with a sick kid, when you don't want to be the person who experimented.
segments.tr: Sie kaufen eine Reduktion von Zweifeln — um 2 Uhr morgens, mit einem kranken Kind, wenn Sie nicht die Person sein wollen, die experimentiert hat.

segments.src: Some of that trust was earned in a specific moment.
segments.tr: Ein Teil dieses Vertrauens wurde in einem bestimmten Moment verdient.

segments.src: In 1982, seven people in the Chicago area died after someone laced Tylenol capsules with cyanide.
segments.tr: 1982 starben sieben Menschen in der Gegend von Chicago, nachdem jemand Tylenol-Kapseln mit Zyanid vergiftet hatte.

segments.src: Johnson & Johnson pulled roughly 31 million bottles nationwide, went public fast, and came back with tamper-evident packaging that became the industry norm.
segments.tr: Johnson & Johnson zog landesweit etwa 31 Millionen Flaschen ein, ging schnell an die Öffentlichkeit und kam mit einer manipulationssicheren Verpackung zurück, die zum Industriestandard wurde.

segments.src: The brand lost most of its share and rebuilt it within about a year.
segments.tr: Die Marke verlor den Großteil ihres Marktanteils und baute ihn innerhalb von etwa einem Jahr wieder auf.

segments.src: That's the double lesson: equity is fragile enough to nearly vanish in a week, and durable enough to be worth defending at enormous cost.
segments.tr: Das ist die doppelte Lektion: Markenwert ist zerbrechlich genug, um fast in einer Woche zu verschwinden, und dauerhaft genug, um es wert zu sein, ihn mit enormen Kosten zu verteidigen.

segments.src: Now look one shelf over at the extensions: Tylenol PM.
segments.tr: Ein Regalfach weiter finden Sie die Erweiterungen: Tylenol PM.

segments.src: Tylenol Cold + Flu.
segments.tr: Tylenol Cold + Flu.

segments.src: Children's Tylenol.
segments.tr: Tylenol für Kinder.

segments.src: Every one of them is the same bet — *you already trust us with your headache, so trust us with your cold.* High perceived fit, so the borrowing works.
segments.tr: Jedes davon ist dieselbe Wette — *Sie vertrauen uns bereits mit Ihrem Kopfschmerz, vertrauen Sie uns also mit Ihrer Erkältung.* Hohe wahrgenommene Passung, daher funktioniert es.

segments.src: Then ask yourself the honest question: would you buy Tylenol-brand energy drinks?
segments.tr: Dann stellen Sie sich die ehrliche Frage: würden Sie Tylenol-Energydrinks kaufen?

segments.src: Same company, same trust, same shelf.
segments.tr: Gleiches Unternehmen, gleiches Vertrauen, gleiches Regal.

segments.src: But the fit collapses, and so would the extension.
segments.tr: Aber die Passung fällt zusammen, und auch die Erweiterung würde es tun.

segments.src: Tylenol means "makes discomfort go away safely."
segments.tr: Tylenol bedeutet "Unbehagen sicher beseitigen."

segments.src: An energy drink means the opposite of sedation.
segments.tr: Ein Energydrink bedeutet das Gegenteil von Sedation.

segments.src: The name would fight the product.
segments.tr: Der Name würde gegen das Produkt kämpfen.

segments.src: ## Three-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## Drei-Zeilen-Zusammenfassung

segments.src: 1. Brand equity is the value the name adds on top of the product — built from awareness, perceived quality, associations, and loyalty.
segments.tr: 1. Markenwert ist der Wert, den der Name zusätzlich zum Produkt hinzufügt — aufgebaut aus Bekanntheit, wahrgenommener Qualität, Assoziationen und Loyalität.

segments.src: 2. Brand identity is what you intend to mean; brand image is what customers actually think you mean, and the gap between them is the job.
segments.tr: 2. Markenidentität ist, was Sie beabsichtigen zu bedeuten; Markenimage ist, was Kunden tatsächlich denken, dass Sie bedeuten, und die Lücke zwischen ihnen ist die Aufgabe.

segments.src: 3. Brand extensions let you spend accumulated equity in a new category — profitable when perceived fit is high, dilutive when it isn't.
segments.tr: 3. Markenerweiterungen lassen Sie angesammelten Markenwert in einer neuen Kategorie ausgeben — profitabel wenn die wahrgenommene Passung hoch ist, verwässernd wenn dies nicht der Fall ist.

segments.src: ## ✅ Self-Quiz
segments.tr: ## ✅ Selbstquiz

segments.src: **1.** A store-brand acetaminophen has the identical active ingredient and dose as the national brand, yet many shoppers pay more for the national brand.
segments.tr: **1.** Ein Acetaminophen der Eigenmarke hat den identischen Wirkstoff und die gleiche Dosis wie das Markenprodukt, dennoch zahlen viele Käufer mehr für das Markenprodukt.

segments.src: This price premium is the clearest everyday evidence of:
segments.tr: Diese Preisprämie ist der klarste alltägliche Beweis für:

segments.src: - A) Product differentiation through formulation
segments.tr: - A) Produktdifferenzierung durch Formulierung

segments.src: - B) Brand equity
segments.tr: - B) Markenwert

segments.src: - C) A distribution advantage
segments.tr: - C) Ein Vertriebsvorteil

segments.src: - D) Regulatory protection
segments.tr: - D) Regulatorischer Schutz

segments.src: **2.** True or False: Brand identity and brand image mean the same thing.
segments.tr: **2.** Wahr oder Falsch: Markenidentität und Markenimage bedeuten dasselbe.

segments.src: **3.** A premium coffee brand launches branded ceramic mugs and travel tumblers.
segments.tr: **3.** Eine Premium-Kaffeemarke startet Marken-Keramiktassen und Reisebecher.

segments.src: Compared with that same brand launching motor oil, the mug launch is more likely to succeed mainly because of:
segments.tr: Verglichen mit dem Start von Motoröl derselben Marke ist der Start der Becher eher erfolgreich, hauptsächlich aufgrund von:

segments.src: - A) Lower manufacturing cost
segments.tr: - A) Niedrigere Herstellungskosten

segments.src: - B) Higher perceived fit with existing brand associations
segments.tr: - B) Höhere wahrgenommene Passung mit bestehenden Markenassoziationen

segments.src: - C) Stronger patent position
segments.tr: - C) Stärkere Patentposition

segments.src: - D) A larger addressable market
segments.tr: - D) Ein größerer adressierbarer Markt

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 Die Begriffe von heute

segments.src: - **Brand equity** — the added value a brand name gives a product beyond its functional attributes, visible as price premium, loyalty, and market power.
segments.tr: - **Markenwert** — der zusätzliche Wert, den ein Markenname einem Produkt über seine funktionalen Eigenschaften hinaus verleiht, sichtbar als Preisprämie, Loyalität und Marktmacht.

segments.src: - **Brand identity** — the meaning and personality the company deliberately builds and wants the brand to stand for.
segments.tr: - **Markenidentität** — die Bedeutung und Persönlichkeit, die das Unternehmen bewusst aufbaut und für die die Marke stehen soll.

segments.src: - **Brand image** — the meaning customers actually hold in their heads, which may differ from the intended identity.
segments.tr: - **Markenimage** — die Bedeutung, die Kunden tatsächlich in ihren Köpfen haben, die sich von der beabsichtigten Identität unterscheiden kann.

segments.src: - **Brand extension** — launching a product in a *new* category under an existing brand name (versus a **line extension**, a new variant inside the same category).
segments.tr: - **Markenerweiterung** — Starten eines Produkts in einer *neuen* Kategorie unter einem bestehenden Markennamen (im Gegensatz zu einer **Linienerweiterung**, eine neue Variante innerhalb der gleichen Kategorie).

segments.src: - **Brand dilution** — the weakening of a brand's core associations, typically caused by extensions that don't fit or by inconsistent quality.
segments.tr: - **Markenverwässerung** — die Abschwächung der Kernassoziationen einer Marke, typischerweise verursacht durch Erweiterungen, die nicht passen, oder durch inkonsistente Qualität.

segments.src: *Answers: **1 — B.** With the active ingredient, dose, and regulatory standard held constant, the leftover willingness to pay is attributable to the name itself; that's the price-premium view of brand equity.
segments.tr: *Antworten: **1 — B.** Bei gleicher Wirkstoff, Dosis und regulatorischem Standard ist die zusätzliche Zahlungsbereitschaft dem Namen selbst zuzuschreiben; das ist die Preisprämien-Sichtweise von Markenwert.

segments.src: **2 — False.** Identity is sender-side (what the firm intends); image is receiver-side (what the customer perceives).
segments.tr: **2 — Falsch.** Identität ist auf der Absenderseite (was das Unternehmen beabsichtigt); Image ist auf der Empfängerseite (was der Kunde wahrnimmt).

segments.src: Managing a brand largely means shrinking the distance between the two.
segments.tr: Eine Marke zu verwalten bedeutet großteils, den Abstand zwischen den beiden zu verringern.

segments.src: **3 — B.** Mugs and tumblers sit naturally inside a coffee brand's existing associations, so consumers transfer trust easily.
segments.tr: **3 — B.** Tassen und Reisebecher passen natürlich zu den bestehenden Assoziationen einer Kaffeemarke, daher übertragen Verbraucher Vertrauen leicht.

segments.src: Motor oil shares no meaningful associations with coffee, so the transfer fails and risks diluting the parent brand.*
segments.tr: Motoröl teilt keine sinnvollen Assoziationen mit Kaffee, daher schlägt die Übertragung fehl und riskiert, die Muttermarke zu verwässern.*

vi.title: [Marketing 101 #11] Tại Sao Cùng Một Viên Thuốc Lại Đắt Gấp Đôi Chỉ Vì Một Cái Tên

segments.src: > A brand is a promise stored in someone's head — and brand management is the work of building that promise, keeping it consistent, and knowing how far you can stretch it before it snaps.
segments.tr: > Thương hiệu là một lời hứa được lưu giữ trong tâm trí của ai đó — và quản lý thương hiệu là công việc xây dựng lời hứa đó, giữ nó nhất quán, và biết bạn có thể kéo dài nó bao xa trước khi nó đổ vỡ.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Khái Niệm Hôm Nay

segments.src: Walk into any store and you'll find two products that are physically close to identical, sitting side by side, with very different price tags.
segments.tr: Bước vào bất kỳ cửa hàng nào và bạn sẽ tìm thấy hai sản phẩm gần như giống hệt nhau về mặt vật lý, xếp cạnh nhau, với các nhãn giá rất khác nhau.

segments.src: Nothing about the atoms explains the gap.
segments.tr: Không có gì về các nguyên tử giải thích được khoảng cách này.

segments.src: Something about the *name* does.
segments.tr: Điều gì đó về *tên* thì có.

segments.src: That gap has a name in marketing: **brand equity** — the extra value a brand name adds beyond what the product itself delivers.
segments.tr: Khoảng cách đó có tên gọi trong tiếp thị: **giá trị thương hiệu** — giá trị bổ sung mà tên thương hiệu thêm vào ngoài những gì sản phẩm tự nó mang lại.

segments.src: One rough way to picture it:
segments.tr: Một cách đơn giản để hình dung nó:

segments.src: Brand equity ≈ what people will pay for the branded version
segments.tr: Brand equity ≈ what people will pay for the branded version

segments.src: − what they'd pay for an identical unbranded version
segments.tr: − what they'd pay for an identical unbranded version

segments.src: That's a simplification (equity also shows up as loyalty, bargaining power with retailers, and cheaper customer acquisition), but it makes the idea concrete: equity is measurable, and it lives in the customer's mind, not on the factory floor.
segments.tr: Đó là một sự đơn giản hóa (giá trị thương hiệu cũng thể hiện như lòng trung thành, sức mạnh mặc cả với nhà bán lẻ, và chi phí thu thập khách hàng thấp hơn), nhưng nó làm cho ý tưởng trở nên cụ thể: giá trị thương hiệu có thể đo lường được, và nó sống trong tâm trí của khách hàng, không phải trên sàn nhà máy.

segments.src: Marketing academics usually break brand equity into four building blocks, following David Aaker's well-known model:
segments.tr: Các học giả tiếp thị thường chia giá trị thương hiệu thành bốn khối xây dựng, theo mô hình nổi tiếng của David Aaker:

segments.src: - **Awareness** — do people know you exist, and do you come to mind first?
segments.tr: - **Nhận Thức** — mọi người có biết bạn tồn tại không, và bạn có xuất hiện trong tâm trí người đó trước tiên không?

segments.src: - **Perceived quality** — do they believe you're good, whether or not lab tests agree?
segments.tr: - **Chất Lượng Cảm Nhận** — họ có tin rằng bạn tốt không, dù các bài kiểm tra phòng thí nghiệm có đồng ý hay không?

segments.src: - **Associations** — what images, feelings, and situations attach to the name?
segments.tr: - **Liên Kết** — những hình ảnh, cảm xúc và tình huống nào gắn liền với tên?

segments.src: - **Loyalty** — will they buy you again when a cheaper option is right there?
segments.tr: - **Lòng Trung Thành** — họ có mua lại từ bạn không khi có một lựa chọn rẻ hơn ngay đó?

segments.src: Now, the second concept.
segments.tr: Bây giờ là khái niệm thứ hai.

segments.src: **Brand identity** is what the company *intends* the brand to stand for — the positioning, the personality, the visual system, the tone.
segments.tr: **Nhận Diện Thương Hiệu** là những gì công ty *có ý định* thương hiệu sẽ đại diện — định vị, tính cách, hệ thống hình ảnh, giọng điệu.

segments.src: **Brand image** is what customers *actually* believe.
segments.tr: **Hình Ảnh Thương Hiệu** là những gì khách hàng *thực sự* tin tưởng.

segments.src: Those two are rarely the same thing, and closing the gap is most of a brand manager's job.
segments.tr: Hai điều đó hiếm khi giống nhau, và việc giảm khoảng cách là phần lớn công việc của một nhà quản lý thương hiệu.

segments.src: You control the identity.
segments.tr: Bạn kiểm soát nhận diện.

segments.src: You only influence the image.
segments.tr: Bạn chỉ ảnh hưởng đến hình ảnh.

segments.src: Third: **brand extension**.
segments.tr: Thứ ba: **mở rộng thương hiệu**.

segments.src: Once a brand has equity, it's tempting to spend it — to launch a product in a new category under the same name and borrow the trust you've already earned.
segments.tr: Khi một thương hiệu có giá trị, việc sử dụng nó là hấp dẫn — để ra mắt một sản phẩm trong một danh mục mới dưới cùng một tên và mượn lòng tin bạn đã kiếm được.

segments.src: Extensions are cheap compared to building a brand from zero, and that's exactly why they're overused.
segments.tr: Các mở rộng rẻ hơn so với xây dựng một thương hiệu từ con số không, và đó chính xác là lý do tại sao chúng bị lạm dụng.

segments.src: The variable that predicts success is **perceived fit**: does the new product feel like something this brand would plausibly make?
segments.tr: Biến số dự đoán thành công là **sự phù hợp cảm nhận**: sản phẩm mới có cảm thấy giống như một cái gì đó mà thương hiệu này có thể tạo ra không?

segments.src: Nike moving from shoes into athletic apparel fits.
segments.tr: Nike chuyển từ giày dép sang quần áo thể thao là phù hợp.

segments.src: Apple moving from computers into phones fits.
segments.tr: Apple chuyển từ máy tính sang điện thoại là phù hợp.

segments.src: Harley-Davidson launching a perfume in the 1990s did not fit, and it's still cited in textbooks as the cautionary tale.
segments.tr: Harley-Davidson ra mắt một loại nước hoa vào những năm 1990 không phù hợp, và nó vẫn được trích dẫn trong sách giáo khoa như một câu chuyện cảnh báo.

segments.src: When fit is weak, the extension usually fails — and worse, it can cause **brand dilution**, muddying the associations that made the parent brand valuable in the first place.
segments.tr: Khi sự phù hợp yếu, mở rộng thường thất bại — và tệ hơn, nó có thể gây ra **làm yếu giá trị thương hiệu**, làm mơ hồ những liên kết đã làm cho thương hiệu cha quý báu ngay từ đầu.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## Trong Cuộc Sống Hàng Ngày

segments.src: Stand in the pain-relief aisle at a CVS or a Walgreens.
segments.tr: Đứng ở khu vực giảm đau tại CVS hoặc Walgreens.

segments.src: On the shelf: Tylenol Extra Strength, 500 mg acetaminophen.
segments.tr: Trên kệ: Tylenol Extra Strength, 500 mg acetaminophen.

segments.src: Next to it: the store's own brand — CVS Health or Walgreens — also 500 mg acetaminophen.
segments.tr: Bên cạnh nó: thương hiệu riêng của cửa hàng — CVS Health hoặc Walgreens — cũng 500 mg acetaminophen.

segments.src: Same active ingredient, same dose, both regulated by the FDA to the same standard.
segments.tr: Cùng một chất hoạt động, cùng một liều lượng, cả hai được FDA điều chỉnh theo cùng một tiêu chuẩn.

segments.src: The store brand often costs noticeably less per caplet; the exact spread moves with sales and store, but a several-dollar gap on a 100-count bottle is typical.
segments.tr: Thương hiệu cửa hàng thường chi phí ít hơn đáng kể cho mỗi viên; mức chênh lệch chính xác thay đổi theo doanh số bán hàng và cửa hàng, nhưng khoảng cách vài đô la trên chai 100 viên là điển hình.

segments.src: Millions of Americans reach for the more expensive one anyway.
segments.tr: Hàng triệu người Mỹ vẫn lựa chọn cái đắt hơn.

segments.src: That decision, repeated at scale, *is* brand equity.
segments.tr: Quyết định đó, lặp lại ở quy mô lớn, *là* giá trị thương hiệu.

segments.src: People aren't buying better chemistry.
segments.tr: Mọi người không mua hóa học tốt hơn.

segments.src: They're buying a reduction in doubt — at 2 a.m., with a sick kid, when you don't want to be the person who experimented.
segments.tr: Họ đang mua sự giảm bớt nghi ngờ — lúc 2 giờ sáng, với một đứa trẻ bệnh, khi bạn không muốn trở thành người thử nghiệm.

segments.src: Some of that trust was earned in a specific moment.
segments.tr: Một số lòng tin đó được kiếm được trong một khoảnh khắc cụ thể.

segments.src: In 1982, seven people in the Chicago area died after someone laced Tylenol capsules with cyanide.
segments.tr: Năm 1982, bảy người ở khu vực Chicago đã chết sau khi ai đó pha chế viên nang Tylenol bằng xyanua.

segments.src: Johnson & Johnson pulled roughly 31 million bottles nationwide, went public fast, and came back with tamper-evident packaging that became the industry norm.
segments.tr: Johnson & Johnson đã rút khoảng 31 triệu chai trên toàn quốc, công khai nhanh chóng, và quay trở lại với bao bì chống giả mạo trở thành tiêu chuẩn ngành.

segments.src: The brand lost most of its share and rebuilt it within about a year.
segments.tr: Thương hiệu đã mất phần lớn thị phần của nó và xây dựng lại nó trong khoảng một năm.

segments.src: That's the double lesson: equity is fragile enough to nearly vanish in a week, and durable enough to be worth defending at enormous cost.
segments.tr: Đó là bài học kép: giá trị thương hiệu đủ mỏng manh để gần như biến mất trong một tuần, và đủ bền để đáng giá được bảo vệ với chi phí khổng lồ.

segments.src: Now look one shelf over at the extensions: Tylenol PM.
segments.tr: Bây giờ nhìn sang một kệ khác ở các mở rộng: Tylenol PM.

segments.src: Tylenol Cold + Flu.
segments.tr: Tylenol Cold + Flu.

segments.src: Children's Tylenol.
segments.tr: Children's Tylenol.

segments.src: Every one of them is the same bet — *you already trust us with your headache, so trust us with your cold.* High perceived fit, so the borrowing works.
segments.tr: Mỗi cái đều là cùng một cược — *bạn đã tin tưởng chúng tôi với đau đầu của bạn, vậy hãy tin tưởng chúng tôi với cảm lạnh của bạn.* Sự phù hợp cảm nhận cao, vì vậy việc mượn có hiệu quả.

segments.src: Then ask yourself the honest question: would you buy Tylenol-brand energy drinks?
segments.tr: Sau đó hỏi chính mình câu hỏi thẳng thắn: bạn có mua nước uống năng lượng hiệu Tylenol không?

segments.src: Same company, same trust, same shelf.
segments.tr: Cùng công ty, cùng lòng tin, cùng kệ.

segments.src: But the fit collapses, and so would the extension.
segments.tr: Nhưng sự phù hợp sụp đổ, và mở rộng cũng vậy.

segments.src: Tylenol means "makes discomfort go away safely."
segments.tr: Tylenol có nghĩa là "giảm bớt sự khó chịu một cách an toàn."

segments.src: An energy drink means the opposite of sedation.
segments.tr: Một nước uống năng lượng có nghĩa là ngược lại với việc thả lỏng.

segments.src: The name would fight the product.
segments.tr: Tên này sẽ xung đột với sản phẩm.

segments.src: ## Three-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## Tóm Tắt Ba Dòng

segments.src: 1. Brand equity is the value the name adds on top of the product — built from awareness, perceived quality, associations, and loyalty.
segments.tr: 1. Giá trị thương hiệu là giá trị mà tên thêm vào ngoài sản phẩm — được xây dựng từ nhận thức, chất lượng cảm nhận, liên kết, và lòng trung thành.

segments.src: 2. Brand identity is what you intend to mean; brand image is what customers actually think you mean, and the gap between them is the job.
segments.tr: 2. Nhận diện thương hiệu là những gì bạn có ý định để có nghĩa; hình ảnh thương hiệu là những gì khách hàng thực sự nghĩ bạn có ý định để có nghĩa, và khoảng cách giữa chúng là công việc.

segments.src: 3. Brand extensions let you spend accumulated equity in a new category — profitable when perceived fit is high, dilutive when it isn't.
segments.tr: 3. Mở rộng thương hiệu cho phép bạn chi tiêu giá trị tích lũy trong một danh mục mới — có lợi nhuận khi sự phù hợp cảm nhận cao, làm yếu khi nó không phải.

segments.src: ## ✅ Self-Quiz
segments.tr: ## ✅ Tự Kiểm Tra

segments.src: **1.** A store-brand acetaminophen has the identical active ingredient and dose as the national brand, yet many shoppers pay more for the national brand.
segments.tr: **1.** Acetaminophen hiệu cửa hàng có cùng một chất hoạt động và liều lượng giống hệt như thương hiệu quốc gia, nhưng nhiều khách hàng trả tiền nhiều hơn cho thương hiệu quốc gia.

segments.src: This price premium is the clearest everyday evidence of:
segments.tr: Mức giá cao hơn này là bằng chứng hàng ngày rõ ràng nhất của:

segments.src: - A) Product differentiation through formulation
segments.tr: - A) Phân biệt sản phẩm thông qua công thức

segments.src: - B) Brand equity
segments.tr: - B) Giá trị thương hiệu

segments.src: - C) A distribution advantage
segments.tr: - C) Lợi thế phân phối

segments.src: - D) Regulatory protection
segments.tr: - D) Bảo vệ pháp lệ

segments.src: **2.** True or False: Brand identity and brand image mean the same thing.
segments.tr: **2.** Đúng hoặc Sai: Nhận diện thương hiệu và hình ảnh thương hiệu có cùng một nghĩa.

segments.src: **3.** A premium coffee brand launches branded ceramic mugs and travel tumblers.
segments.tr: **3.** Một thương hiệu cà phê cao cấp ra mắt những chiếc cốc gốm có nhãn hiệu và cốc du lịch.

segments.src: Compared with that same brand launching motor oil, the mug launch is more likely to succeed mainly because of:
segments.tr: So với khi cùng thương hiệu đó ra mắt dầu động cơ, cuộc ra mắt chiếc cốc có khả năng thành công hơn chủ yếu vì:

segments.src: - A) Lower manufacturing cost
segments.tr: - A) Chi phí sản xuất thấp hơn

segments.src: - B) Higher perceived fit with existing brand associations
segments.tr: - B) Sự phù hợp cảm nhận cao hơn với những liên kết thương hiệu hiện có

segments.src: - C) Stronger patent position
segments.tr: - C) Vị trí bằng sáng chế mạnh hơn

segments.src: - D) A larger addressable market
segments.tr: - D) Một thị trường có thể tiếp cận lớn hơn

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 Các Thuật Ngữ Hôm Nay

segments.src: - **Brand equity** — the added value a brand name gives a product beyond its functional attributes, visible as price premium, loyalty, and market power.
segments.tr: - **Giá Trị Thương Hiệu** — giá trị bổ sung mà tên thương hiệu mang lại cho một sản phẩm ngoài các thuộc tính chức năng của nó, thể hiện dưới dạng mức giá cao hơn, lòng trung thành, và sức mạnh thị trường.

segments.src: - **Brand identity** — the meaning and personality the company deliberately builds and wants the brand to stand for.
segments.tr: - **Nhận Diện Thương Hiệu** — ý nghĩa và tính cách mà công ty cố ý xây dựng và muốn thương hiệu đại diện.

segments.src: - **Brand image** — the meaning customers actually hold in their heads, which may differ from the intended identity.
segments.tr: - **Hình Ảnh Thương Hiệu** — ý nghĩa mà khách hàng thực sự giữ trong tâm trí họ, có thể khác với nhận diện có ý định.

segments.src: - **Brand extension** — launching a product in a *new* category under an existing brand name (versus a **line extension**, a new variant inside the same category).
segments.tr: - **Mở Rộng Thương Hiệu** — ra mắt một sản phẩm trong một danh mục *mới* dưới tên thương hiệu hiện có (so với **mở rộng dòng sản phẩm**, một biến thể mới bên trong cùng một danh mục).

segments.src: - **Brand dilution** — the weakening of a brand's core associations, typically caused by extensions that don't fit or by inconsistent quality.
segments.tr: - **Làm Yếu Giá Trị Thương Hiệu** — sự suy yếu các liên kết cốt lõi của một thương hiệu, thường do mở rộng không phù hợp hoặc do chất lượng không nhất quán.

segments.src: *Answers: **1 — B.** With the active ingredient, dose, and regulatory standard held constant, the leftover willingness to pay is attributable to the name itself; that's the price-premium view of brand equity.
segments.tr: *Câu Trả Lời: **1 — B.** Với chất hoạt động, liều lượng, và tiêu chuẩn pháp lệ được giữ nguyên, mong muốn chi trả còn lại có thể được quy cho tên gọi chính nó; đó là quan điểm mức giá cao hơn của giá trị thương hiệu.

segments.src: **2 — False.** Identity is sender-side (what the firm intends); image is receiver-side (what the customer perceives).
segments.tr: **2 — Sai.** Nhận diện là phía người gửi (những gì công ty có ý định); hình ảnh là phía người nhận (những gì khách hàng cảm nhận).

segments.src: Managing a brand largely means shrinking the distance between the two.
segments.tr: Quản lý một thương hiệu phần lớn có nghĩa là thu hẹp khoảng cách giữa hai cái.

segments.src: **3 — B.** Mugs and tumblers sit naturally inside a coffee brand's existing associations, so consumers transfer trust easily.
segments.tr: **3 — B.** Những chiếc cốc và cốc du lịch nằm một cách tự nhiên bên trong những liên kết thương hiệu cà phê hiện có, vì vậy người tiêu dùng chuyển lòng tin dễ dàng.

segments.src: Motor oil shares no meaningful associations with coffee, so the transfer fails and risks diluting the parent brand.*
segments.tr: Dầu động cơ không chia sẻ bất kỳ liên kết nào có ý nghĩa với cà phê, vì vậy chuyển lạc bại và có nguy cơ làm yếu thương hiệu cha.*
